# LLM Prefill & Decode Speed Visualizer

An interactive tool for understanding LLM inference performance: prefill (compute-bound prompt ingestion, sets TTFT) vs decode (bandwidth-bound token generation, sets TPOT), across single-turn chat and multi-turn agentic loops.

## For AI agents — read this first

Everything on the page is available as plain JSON over HTTP. No browser needed.

Base URL: https://llm-prefill-decode-visualizer.vercel.app
OpenAPI spec: /api/spec (machine-readable, derive all endpoints from it)

### URL versioning (/v1/)

Every endpoint below is also served under a versioned prefix: replace `/api/` with `/v1/` (e.g. `/v1/compute?model=singleTurn&…`, `/v1/benchmarks`, `/v1/spec`). The two prefixes are identical — same handlers, same responses, same rate limits.

- **External consumers should harden onto `/v1/`.** It gives us room to ship breaking changes under a new prefix without silently breaking your integration.
- The unversioned `/api/*` paths keep working and remain where the docs live (`/api/spec`).
- Policy: additive changes never break existing clients; breaking changes ship under a new version prefix and the previous one is kept for at least 90 days with `Deprecation`/`Sunset` headers (see CHANGELOG-API.md in the repo for the full schema-versioning policy).

**GET /api/health** — liveness + upstream data freshness ({ok, upstreamFreshness, cacheAge}). Human status page at /status.html.

### Endpoints

**GET /api/compute?model=<name>&<params>** — run any simulator math and get exact numbers.

Models:
- `singleTurn` — TTFT, TPOT, total walltime for a chat request. Params: `promptTokens`, `outputTokens`, `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`.
  Example: `/api/compute?model=singleTurn&promptTokens=4096&outputTokens=512&prefillSpeed=3800&decodeSpeed=105`
- `speculative` — effective decode speed with a draft model. Params: `baseDecodeSpeed`, `draftTokens`, `acceptanceRate`, `draftCostFraction`.
- `batched` — per-user vs aggregate throughput at batch size B (per-user decode decays ~B^0.25). Params: `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`, `batchSize`, `promptTokens`, `outputTokens`.
- `agentic` — turn-by-turn walltime for a tool-calling loop, with/without prefix caching savings. Params: `numTurns`, `basePromptTokens`, `toolOutputTokensPerTurn`, `decodeTokensPerTurn`, `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`, `enablePrefixCaching`.
- `kvCache` — KV-cache VRAM for an architecture. Params: `architecture` (`llama70b|llama8b|qwen72b|mistral7b`) or explicit `numLayers`+`kvHeads`+`headDim`, plus `contextLength`, `precisionBytes` (2=FP16, 1=FP8, 0.5=INT4), `batchSize`.
- `flagged` — engine launch-flag modeling. Params: `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`, `promptTokens`, `outputTokens`, and `flags` (comma-separated ids: `flash-attn,kv-q8,kv-q4,no-mmap,vllm-fp8-kv,vllm-o3`). Returns adjusted speeds, a per-flag audit trail (delta + source note), warnings, and a `singleTurn` simulation at the adjusted speeds. Deltas are documented heuristics, not measurements.
- `cost` — $/1M tokens for owned hardware: amortized purchase price + electricity over the measured speeds of a scenario shape. Params: `hardwarePriceUsd`, `electricityRatePerKwh` (default 0.15), `powerDrawWatts`, `amortizationMonths` (default 36), plus the usual `promptTokens`, `outputTokens`, `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`.
  Example: `/api/compute?model=cost&hardwarePriceUsd=2000&powerDrawWatts=450&electricityRatePerKwh=0.15&prefillSpeed=3800&decodeSpeed=105`

**GET /api/vram** — combined model + KV-cache + context VRAM from just an `hfId`. Architecture (layers, hidden dim, GQA heads, head dim) and weight size are resolved from the Hugging Face config automatically — you never look up model internals.
- `/api/vram?hfId=meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct&context=65536&quant=q4_k_m` → weights GB + KV GB + total, with the resolved architecture and the KV bytes/token formula.
- Add `&vramGb=24` → `fits` flag plus `maxContextTokens` that fit the budget (upper bound; ignores activation overhead).
- Add `&numTurns=40&tokensPerTurn=1200` → per-turn KV-growth projection with the exact turn where the context window (`firstContextOverflowTurn`) or VRAM budget (`firstVramOverflowTurn`) is first exceeded.
- `quant` accepts GGUF/GPTQ tags (fp16, fp8, q8_0, q6_k, q5_k_m, q4_k_m, q4_0, q3_k_m, q2_k…); unknown tags assume ~4-bit and set `inputs.quantAssumed: true`.
- GGUF-only repos (no safetensors metadata) fall back to the largest `.gguf` file size for weight VRAM.
- Resolution is three-tier (check `model.resolutionSource`): `builtin-table` — common families (llama*, qwen3*, gemma*, mistral*) resolve offline from a built-in config table, no huggingface.co call; `huggingface` — everything else resolves from the repo's config.json / GGUF header; `name-heuristic` — when HF is unreachable or gated but the model name carries a size tag ("Foo-13B"), a coarse bucketed estimate is returned with the assumption spelled out in `model.notes`. Bad ids still 404.

Calling `/api/compute` with no `model` returns a self-describing capability list.

**Batching (one round trip for N comparisons):** `POST /api/compute` with `{"batch": [{"model": "singleTurn", "promptTokens": 4096}, {"model": "kvCache", "architecture": "llama70b", "contextLength": 131072}]}` (also accepted as `variants`, or `?batch=[...]` as URL-encoded JSON on GET). Each item is a normal parameter set including its own `model` field; max 50 items. Response: `{batch: true, count, okCount, errorCount, results: [{index, ok, result | error}]}` — one bad scenario returns a per-item error instead of failing the whole batch.

**Dry-run / sandbox (`dry_run=true`):** add `&dry_run=true` to any `/api/compute` call (or `"dry_run": true` in the POST body; also applies per-item inside a batch) to validate the request and echo the parsed parameters — defaults filled in, numbers coerced — WITHOUT executing any math. Response: `{dry_run: true, model, inputs, id?, note}`. The `id` is the same deterministic hash the real call would return, and failures (unknown model, malformed batch) behave exactly as they would for a real call — use it as a cheap sanity check before spending a real computation. Example: `/api/compute?model=agentic&numTurns=6&enablePrefixCaching=true&dry_run=true`.

Every `/api/compute` and `/api/best` response carries a deterministic `id` (`calc_<12 hex chars>`) hashed from the resolved request. Cite it to reference a result across turns:

**GET /api/calc/<id>?<original params>** — replay any computation from its id. Ids are pure content hashes, not database keys: resend the original parameters and the endpoint re-runs identical math and stamps `verified: true`. Example:
- `/api/compute?model=singleTurn&promptTokens=4096` → `{ "id": "calc_x", ... }`
- `/api/calc/calc_x?model=singleTurn&promptTokens=4096` → same numbers, `verified: true`
- For `/api/best` results add `endpoint=best`: `/api/calc/calc_y?endpoint=best&by=decode&maxParamsB=8`
- Altered parameters are rejected with `expected` = the id they actually hash to.

**GET /api/presets** — built-in hardware speed presets (RTX 4090, dual 3090, M3 Ultra, Groq, H100, RPi5…) and workload scenarios (RAG query, code generation…). Use these as `/api/compute` inputs.

**GET /api/localmaxxing** — community-measured single-stream benchmark runs (3,600+).
- No params: hardware-group summary (71 rigs, run counts).
- `?hardware=rtx 3090&limit=50`: runs for rigs matching that substring.
- `?model=qwen3.6-27b&limit=20`: runs for a model. `model` matches the **normalized family** — repo/quant/finetune variants collapse (`unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF` and `mlx-community/Qwen3.6-27B-4bit` are both `qwen3.6-27b`).
- `?quant=q4_k_m`: exact quantization filter.
- Filtered calls are cursor-paginated: `{ total, items[], has_more, next_cursor }`, sorted by decode speed desc (runId tiebreak). Page size: `limit` (default 50, max 500). Follow `next_cursor` until `has_more` is false; cursors stay stable even when new runs land mid-scan.

**POST /api/localmaxxing** — submit a community benchmark run for review. JSON body with required `model`, `quant`, `hardware`, `hwClass` (`discrete_gpu|unified|cpu_only`), `prefillTokPerSec`, `decodeTokPerSec`; optional `engine`, token counts, `provenance` (`engineVersion`, `command`, `sourceUrl`, `notes`) and `submitter`. Server-side validation enforces sanity bounds per hardware class (a claimed 99,999 tok/s on an RPi5 is rejected) and rejects near-duplicates of existing runs (same model family + quant + rig within 10%). Valid submissions return `202` with a `submissionId` and are queued for manual review — they never publish immediately. Validation failures return `400` with machine-readable errors: `{"error":"validation_failed","errors":[{"field","code","message"}]}`.

**GET /api/benchmarks** — aggregated stats: median + IQR per group (outlier-resistant). Default groups by hardware×model-family; regroup with `?groupBy=hardware|model|quant`. Each group carries median/q1/q3/min/max for prefill and decode plus the single best measured run. Cursor-paginated like /api/localmaxxing: `{ total, items[], has_more, next_cursor }`, sorted by median decode desc (group key tiebreak); page size `limit` (default 25, max 200).

**GET /api/diff?runA=<id>&runB=<id>** — diff two measured runs in one call: both runs' metrics plus per-metric deltas, ratios (B ÷ A) and a plain-language summary. Time metrics are normalized to a 2048-token prompt / 512-token output.

**GET /api/diff?mode=whatif&a=<constraints>&b=<constraints>** — what-if decision diffing: pass two /api/best-style constraint sets and get back only the deltas — options entering/leaving the feasible set (`entered` / `left`, with rank positions) and per-option VRAM headroom change (`headroom`, from the estimated fit math; enable `fitCheck`/`contextLength` in the sets). Constraint sets accept JSON (`?a={"fitCheck":"true","contextLength":8192}`) or URL-encoded query strings (`?a=fitCheck=true&contextLength=8192`), or a POST body `{"mode":"whatif","a":{...},"b":{...}}`. Example: `/api/diff?mode=whatif&a=fitCheck=true&contextLength=8192&model=qwen&b=fitCheck=true&contextLength=65536&model=qwen` shows which rigs survive a 64k-context requirement and how much headroom the survivors lose.

**GET /api/best** — ranked answers to natural questions:
- `/api/best?by=decode&maxParamsB=8&quant=q4_k_m` → top rigs for ≤8B models at Q4_K_M
- `/api/best?by=prefill&hwClass=unified` → fastest prefill on unified-memory systems
- `/api/best?model=qwen3.6-27b` → fastest rigs for that model family
- `/api/best?model=qwen3.6-27b&fitCheck=true&contextLength=65536` → fastest rigs whose VRAM can actually hold it at 64k context (estimated: weights from params × quant bits + KV cache + 10% overhead)

**GET /api/sizing** — one-call deployment recommendation for agents. Pass a workload spec, get ranked hardware with the math attached:
- `/api/sizing?model=qwen&contextLength=32768&concurrency=4&maxTtftSeconds=2&maxTpotMs=50&maxVramGb=48`
- Each recommendation carries `vramFit` (weights from params × bits-per-weight + KV cache at target context × concurrency + overhead vs available VRAM/unified memory), `expected` TTFT/TPOT from aggregated benchmark medians with IQR, `confidence` from sample count, and `meetsSlo` flags. Ranked meet-SLO-first, then by median per-user decode.
- `/api/best?by=cost&price=2000&electricityRate=0.15` → best tok/s-per-dollar. Ranks by **$/1M tokens** (lower is better): rig price amortized over `amortizationMonths` (default 36) + electricity at `electricityRate` $/kWh (default 0.15) and a per-hwClass power estimate (override with `powerWatts`), divided by effective throughput at median speeds for the scenario shape (`promptTokens`/`outputTokens`, default 2048/512). Each result carries its `costInputs` echo so you can see exactly what was assumed.

### Statistical caveats (machine-readable)

`/api/localmaxxing`, `/api/benchmarks` and `/api/best` all return a top-level `caveats` array — objects with `code`, `severity`, `summary`, `detail`. Don't quote benchmark numbers without checking it. Codes:

- `single_stream_only` — dataset only contains batchSize=1 / concurrency≤1 runs; not batched-serving throughput.
- `self_reported_unvalidated` — community-submitted runs, not independently verified; trust medians over single runs.
- `n1_groups` / `n1_group` — some groups (or this row) rest on a single run; treat as anecdotal. Carries `pct`, `groupsWithOneRun`, `totalGroups`.
- `mixed_engines` — a group or the matched set blends different inference engines (llama.cpp vs MLX vs vLLM…).

`/api/best` and `/api/benchmarks` rows also carry a per-row `caveats` array (`n1_group`, `mixed_engines`) when they apply to that specific group.

**GET /api/snapshots** — versioned dataset snapshot IDs (e.g. `snapshot-2026-08-21-a1b2c3d4`). Every data endpoint response carries a `snapshot` object; pass its ID back as `?snapshot=<id>` on `/api/localmaxxing`, `/api/benchmarks` or `/api/best` to pin the dataset and get reproducible numbers. Unknown/expired IDs fall back to current data with `snapshot.served: false`.

Every result includes a `pricing` object: USD street-price estimate (`estimateUsd`, `lowUsd`, `highUsd`), `perGpu` breakdown when gpuCount > 1, an `asOf` date (prices are curated estimates, not live quotes), and `links.ebay` / `links.ebayUsed` / `links.craigslist` search URLs so a budget constraint can be verified against live listings. `pricing` is `null` for cpu_only rigs and unknown GPUs.

### Typical agent workflow

1. `GET /api/sizing?model=<family>&contextLength=…&concurrency=…&maxTpotMs=…` → ranked hardware recommendations with VRAM fit and expected latency, in one call.
1. `GET /api/vram?hfId=<model>&context=<tokens>&vramGb=<budget>` → will it fit, and at what max context? (no model internals needed).
2. `GET /api/best?by=decode&maxParamsB=8` → find the fastest measured hardware for a model class.
3. `GET /api/presets` for canonical speed numbers, or take medians from `/api/benchmarks` for real-world numbers.
4. `GET /api/compute?model=singleTurn&prefillSpeed=...&decodeSpeed=...&promptTokens=...&outputTokens=...` → walltime/TTFT/TPOT for a specific request shape.
5. Compare variants with one call: `POST /api/compute` with `{"batch": [{...}, {...}]}` (up to 50 parameter sets, per-item ok/error status).
6. Citing an answer? Quote the `snapshot.id` from the data response (and re-pin with `?snapshot=<id>`) so the numbers are reproducible later.

All endpoints return JSON, support CORS, need no auth, and set cache headers (10 min on data endpoints).

### Rate limits

Every `/api/*` response carries rate-limit headers so agents can self-throttle:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit` — requests allowed per 60s window per client (currently **120**).
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining` — requests left in the current window.
- `X-RateLimit-Reset` — Unix epoch seconds when the window resets.
- When exhausted, endpoints return **429** with a `Retry-After` header (seconds) and a JSON body explaining the budget. Back off for that many seconds instead of retrying immediately.

Budget: 120 requests/min per client IP. Note this is enforced best-effort **per serverless instance**: Vercel functions share no memory across invocations, so concurrent warm instances each allow 120/min and cold starts reset counters — treat the limit as a floor on good behavior, not a hard global cap.

### Schema versioning

Every JSON response carries a top-level `schema_version` field (currently `"1"`) and an `X-Schema-Version: 1` header (also on errors and OPTIONS). Additive changes never bump the version; breaking changes bump the major version and are announced ≥90 days ahead via `Deprecation`, `Sunset`, and `Link; rel="deprecation"` headers. Policy + changelog: /CHANGELOG-API.md in the repo.

### Errors (RFC 9457 problem+json)

Every error response is a single problem object served as `application/problem+json`:

```json
{"type": ".../problems/invalid-params", "title": "Invalid parameters", "status": 400, "detail": "Unknown model 'nope'", "instance": "/api/compute?model=nope", "code": "INVALID_PARAMS"}
```

Branch on the stable `code`, never on `title`/`detail` prose:

| code | HTTP | meaning | retry? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_PARAMS` | 400 | bad or missing parameters — fix the input | no (fix first) |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | referenced resource does not exist (reserved) | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | too many requests; honor `Retry-After` | yes, after wait |
| `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` | 502 | community-benchmark source temporarily down | yes, with backoff |
| `INTERNAL` | 500 | unexpected server error | maybe |

The machine-readable registry also lives in `/api/spec` (`x-error-codes` + the `Problem` schema) for generated SDKs. Batch items in `/api/compute` carry per-item `code` alongside the human-readable `error` string.

### Interactive page

The human-facing UI is this same site. Deep links carry state via URL params: `?tab=single|agentic|compare|kvcache|theory`, `preset=<hardware-id>`, `prompt=`, `output=`, `spec=1&draftK=&acc=`. Keyboard: Space play/pause, R reset, 1–5 tabs.

Source: https://github.com/riceharvest/llm-prefill-decode-visualizer
